components.name: Universal Modder
components.scope_note: Local CLI installed by default for every selected provider. Pinned MIT source, offline wheel and one canonical skill routing to twelve upstream guides. UABS pins Pillow/NumPy/PyYAML, packages the knowledge snapshot (the indexed knowledge snapshot), discovers native Windows Steam roots from the registry, never echoes matched credentials and prints a sha256 fingerprint plus key length where `um fal key status` used to print the first and last key characters (CodeQL py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data); the wheel carries a +uabs local version so a refresh reinstalls over an older 0.2.0. The audited refresh adds quoted multi-word knowledge search, ranked hits and broken-link diagnostics while retaining local ComfyUI generation, SHA-256-checked ffmpeg setup and collision-safe backups. No upstream session hook or fal MCP is registered. CLI processing is free/local; fal generation requires user-owned credentials and paid service authorization. FFmpeg/Blender and a real game are separate prerequisites for video/rendering/runtime verification. 2026-10-13 source refresh adds Bannerlord, MT Framework, Hedgehog and Black Rock discovery plus a mod-porting reference; preserves UABS dependency pins, native Steam discovery and credential-safe output. 2026-10-18 source refresh (38 upstream commits, 23902ef) adds Isaac, Just Cause 3/Avalanche, Space Marine 2, Project Zomboid and S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2 knowledge notes, fal keys through the desktop keyring with a masked status command, and a UTF-8 tool-output fix on Windows. Upstream's new agents/ team plus its OpenCode/session files stay unshipped, and the refresh tool now drops the unbounded UE3 unpack_upk.py fallback by rule instead of by hand.

components.name: UABS Toolbox (project tools on demand)
components.scope_note: Bundle-owned, always-on MCP server with three tools (find, describe, call). Task servers stay out of every chat; the toolbox starts the one a task needs on first use, in the same chat, from the bundle's own catalog (toolbox-profiles.json, a copy of PROFILES.json) and the exact entries Set-McpProfile.ps1 -Park saved (parked-mcp.json). Nothing is written to any provider config at call time. Credentials in a parked entry start its server and are never printed. Gate: TESTS/test_toolbox.py (fixture child server; find/describe/call, env pass-through without secret output, project-bound sets, crash restart, TOML parked entries, duplicate suppression).

mcp_tool_budget.mechanism: Hermes tools.include/tools.exclude filter at tool registration; fnmatch globs are supported. Codex has native enabled_tools/disabled_tools; Claude Code supports deferred Tool Search. These sets describe Hermes selections, not a universal provider surface or a bill.
mcp_tool_budget.measurement_basis: Historical sum of per-tool UTF-8 JSON bytes, excluding array framing. Legacy *_tokens_per_turn fields are bytes/4 schema estimates; saving_pct is a schema-size reduction, not measured billed savings.

Full.why: No filter. Every tool registered. Use when authoring records in bulk and diagnosing in the same session.

Lean.why: Drops the three dedicated creation/NIF-mutation/world-placement tools whose parameter schemas carry deep nested objects: housecarl_create (19,198 B), housecarl_nif_set (9,285 B) and housecarl_place (6,975 B) are 35,458 bytes between them -- 22% of the server, and more than the whole of Skyrim Forge. Keeps housecarl_apply for normal patch edits. This is the shipped default because it costs no capability a normal diagnosis or patch-editing session uses.

ReadOnly.why: Everything that reads, diagnoses, validates or looks up, and nothing that writes. Keeps load-order truth, conflict trees, cross-plugin queries, script/dialogue validation, the SKSE audit and the whole keyless Nexus surface. Drops the 14 write tools. Use for diagnosis, load-order work and Nexus research.

mcp_tool_budget.restore: hermes -p skyrim mcp configure housecarl  (interactive checklist, rewrites tools.include). Re-running the migrator will not undo a hand-edited filter.

components.name: Blender MCP
components.scope_note: Talks to an addon inside a running Blender. Pinned: `uvx blender-mcp` was version-free through 7.9.6, and an unpinned invocation can change its tool surface mid-session. `uvx mcp-for-blender@2.0.0 install-addon` places the addon, but ENABLING it is inside the editor and cannot be done from outside that process -- so the profile prints the step rather than claiming it ran it. Note the difference between 'the MCP executable starts' and 'the addon is connected': the server answers initialize with no Blender running at all, and only a tool call that reaches the scene proves the second. Blender is discovered from %APPDATA%\Blender Foundation, which Blender creates on first run whatever the install source -- 7.9.6 carried a maintainer's own Steam drive path here, which could never match on another machine. Measured 2026-09-17 with telemetry disabled and safe mode enabled: 2.0.0 answers initialize/tools-list with 31 tools and 35,646 schema bytes (~8,912 schema tokens (bytes/4; actual usage unmeasured)). The profile writes BLENDER_MCP_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true and BLENDER_MCP_SAFE_MODE=true. Safe mode keeps normal bpy/bmesh/mathutils scene, render, save and import/export work while rejecting eval/exec/open, os/subprocess/network, persistence hooks and external .blend datablock loading before code reaches Blender. components.name: RTK (Rust Token Killer)
components.scope_note: CLI output filter with zero standing schema tokens. GIT CORPUS, measured on this repo AT rtk 1.1.0 against pinned refs: git diff v8.6.1..v8.6.5 430,285 -> 55,870 bytes (87%), git log v8.6.1..v8.6.5 14,250 -> 1,660 (88%), git diff v8.6.4..v8.6.5 33,453 -> 26,820 (20%), and git log --stat -20 v8.6.5 102,301 -> 102,301 (0%). Those are summaries, not lossless replacements: on the larger diff RTK retained 341 of 5,856 changed lines and omitted 5,515. Exact short status is different: a fixture covering staged, unstaged, deleted, renamed, Unicode and untracked paths was line-identical 5/5. NON-GIT CORPUS measured at 0.46.0 on 2026-08-27: rtk test kept the failure at about 93% saved; excluding truncating rows, the aggregate was 7.4% against git's 85.2%. TRUNCATION IS NOT SAVING: rtk json returned one of 5,425 array rows plus `... +5424 more`. rtk find works with a simple -name but breaks on compound predicates; rtk-ai/rtk#3410 reports its unconditional rewrite also intercepts find -delete/-exec. Archive correction: rtk test writes a complete tee for the measured 5.4 KB run and prints its path, but RTK documents a 1 MB raw tee cap. WINDOWS INTEGRATION, re-probed at 0.47.0 on 2026-09-02: upstream rewrite still catches lossy diff/log/show, broken find, cat/read, grep, curl, gh, and mutating git add/commit/push. Therefore broad upstream init and Hermes rtk-rewrite stay off. The bundle installs RTK by default and wires its own allowlist: exact standalone git status plus standalone human-facing pytest, cargo test and go test. Machine-readable output, pipes/redirection, all mutating Git, diff/show/log/find/search/read/curl/gh stay raw. Claude, Grok and Hermes receive the executable hook; Codex and Kimi receive the same narrow instruction because no trusted command-mutation hook is established there. Telemetry remains opt-in. Remeasured 2026-10-02 with TESTS/test_rtk_candidate.py: all four pinned corpus rows; allowlisted rewrite protocol exit 3 PASS; --short/-s preserved staged, unstaged, deleted, renamed, Unicode and untracked status lines (status comparison is line-wise). Broad hooks remain disabled; these are byte savings, not measured billed tokens. 2026-10-13: Apache-2.0 OSS edition selected explicitly; upstream's default binary now uses different licensing. Official Windows OSS archive SHA-256 verified, all four fixed corpus rows unchanged, exact short-status fixture PASS and allowlisted rewrite exit-3 protocol PASS. 2026-10-25: 1.1.0 OSS Windows archive SHA-256 verified, exact short-status fixture PASS and allowlisted rewrite exit-3 protocol PASS. No pipelines, daemon or upstream broad hook enabled.

components.name: OMNI (context distillation)
components.scope_note: CLI + host hook, zero standing tokens -- same slot as rtk, different mechanism, so they stack rather than compete: rtk filters ONE command's output, OMNI remembers output across calls and returns a handle instead of resending what the agent already saw. USE THE README'S NUMBERS, NOT THE LANDING PAGE'S. The page headlines '97.2% off a file read twice' and '~24%'; the README's own corpus of 9,478 executions says '1.4% from the filters, 5.1% with the ledger'. 97.2% is a best case for one re-read, not an expected value -- treat 5% as the number and anything above it as a bonus. Ships a real x86_64-pc-windows-msvc binary with SHA256SUMS (v0.7.8, 2026-08-25), which is why it is here and lowfat is not: lowfat v0.8.0 publishes darwin and linux-gnu only and integrates through a POSIX shell eval hook, the same native-Windows degradation this catalog already documents for rtk's non-Hermes hooks. Full host rewrite on Claude Code, Codex CLI and Gemini CLI; Hermes is supported; MCP-only fallback elsewhere. Stores a local SQLite ledger (permanent project knowledge, 30-day working data, 7-day verbatim traces) -- it is a cache of your own tool output, so treat it as project data, not a temp file. REWIND CAP, measured 2026-08-26 at 0.7.8: output above 65,536 bytes is truncated and NOT archived -- the marker says `full output not archived` and those bytes are unrecoverable, which the README's byte-for-byte guarantee does not qualify. Below the cap the guarantee holds and is self-verifying: the retrieve handle IS the content's SHA-256 prefix, and a 33,453-byte diff came back byte-identical. Head-to-head on this repo's git corpus: rtk 85.2%, OMNI 71.2% headline but only 6.4% once the truncated rows are excluded -- consistent with OMNI's own published 8.8% on git. Its value is the ledger, not the filter; see docs/TOOL-EVALUATIONS.md. Not auto-installed: a 5% saving does not justify rewriting every tool result on a machine by default.
components.compatibility_hold: 2026-10-26: informational evaluation pin 0.7.11 only, not installed or enabled by the bundle. Upstream 0.7.12 (released 2026-10-22) has not been remeasured; the historical ledger/rewind findings must not be presented as measurements of 0.7.11 or 0.7.12.

components.name: Windows MCP
components.scope_note: Desktop control through UI Automation: click, type, send shortcuts, run PowerShell, read and write the registry and the filesystem, enumerate windows and processes. This is the one operating surface the pack had no way to reach -- Playwright and chrome-devtools stop at the browser. UIA also lets an agent PERCEIVE controls without spending a vision call, which is most of why it earns its schema. Measured 2026-08-27 with TOOLS\Measure-McpSchemaCost.ps1 against `uvx windows-mcp@0.8.5 serve`: 20 tools, 22,088 bytes, ~5,522 schema tokens (bytes/4; actual usage unmeasured) -- less than firecrawl-mcp's 36,337 and about four times context7, for the whole desktop. OFF by default and never auto-detected: the `windows` profile carries no detect markers, so -Auto cannot reach it. Turn it on deliberately with TOOLS\Set-McpProfile.ps1 -Enable windows -Global. controls_machine is why TOOLS/measure_mcp_capability.py refuses to sweep it: that sweep calls every advertised tool with arguments synthesized from the schema, which here means typing into whatever window has focus and running whatever PowerShell the sample produces. Update measured 2026-09-28 at 0.8.6: initialize/tools-list PASS, 20 tools, 22,984 compact schema bytes (~5,746 bytes/4 estimate, not billing). Python >=3.14 is now required: the uvx command explicitly selects managed Python 3.14. OFF-by-default scope is unchanged; no desktop actions were invoked. 2026-10-02 refresh: 0.8.7 with Python 3.14: initialize/tools-list PASS; 20 tools, 22,984 compact UTF-8 schema bytes. Still manually opt-in/OFF by default; no desktop actions invoked. Schema bytes are transport measurements, not billed-token savings. 2026-10-10: 0.8.8 Windows initialize/tools-list PASS; 21 advertised tools, 23,545 compact UTF-8 schema bytes (transport bytes, not billed tokens). components.name: Super MCP Router
components.scope_note: A proxy MCP. It registers ONE server carrying discovery/meta-tools and puts every other server behind on-demand discovery: search_tools by intent, get_tool_details for one schema, use_tool to call it. Measured 2026-08-27: 11 tools, 11,386 bytes, ~2,846 meta-tool schema tokens (bytes/4), excluding discovered schemas, results and provider billing. The comparison that matters: houseCARL wired directly is 45 tools, 167,072 bytes, ~41,768 full-schema tokens by the same heuristic. Correction 2026-09-08: Codex has native enabled_tools/disabled_tools filters; Claude Code supports deferred Tool Search. The earlier universal all-tools-every-turn comparison was wrong; no billed saving was measured. Proven end to end against this pack's own houseCARL on 2026-08-27: search_tools('list the plugins in the active load order') -> get_tool_details (3,652 chars, ~913 tokens for that ONE schema) -> use_tool returned live data from the shim (2,999 mods, 2,995 plugins). Startup 1.2s, search 400ms, detail 200ms. NOT wired into a profile, and the reason is specific rather than cautious: the router reads its own config at %USERPROFILE%\.super-mcp\config.json, so enabling it means this pack writing and preserving a THIRD-PARTY tool's config file -- a second config writer with its own merge obligations, on a 24-star dependency. The measurement is what ships here; the wiring is its own release. One caveat to carry into that decision: BM25 ranking returned housecarl_merge_plugins FIRST for that read-only query, with the correct housecarl_load_order_status third. Discovery works, but the top hit is not automatically the safe one. 2026-10-02: candidate 2.8.3 initialize/tools-list PASS in a disposable home, 12 meta-tools and 12,475 compact UTF-8 schema bytes. No child-server routing/config migration was tested; remains unregistered and opt-in.

build_tools.policy: Reuse installed toolchains and install missing capabilities. Update shared stable tools in place through their vendor updater or checksum-verified official Go archive; preserve newer/development SDKs, project pins and user settings. Go swaps retain the previous SDK and roll back a failed publish. -NoUpdate disables upgrades; -CheckOnly and -Offline do not install or update.
